Memory 0.6.0 re-delivers the IDENTICAL MemoryAnalysisRequest only on lease reclaim / authority-transient retry of the same batch; every executor failure creates a new batch whose request_hash, attempt, job_id and idempotency_key all change while the evidence set stays the same (or grows). Second facet: with a non-streaming OpenAI-compatible chat/completions endpoint the provider response id is only known once the response arrived, the Host reconciliation adapter is a constant STILL_UNKNOWN and the SDK never replays, so `sent_unknown -> sent_confirmed` has NO executable production path; AC-2 (3)'s 'unknown then confirmed by provider response id' branch is exercisable only through an injected test reconciliation observer. conclusion.summary: Parent finding confirmed and sharpened by spike: under frozen SDK 0.7.1 neither per-turn hiding nor route-aware projection can turn a standalone-route PROJECT_EFFECT call or a hidden-tool call into a model-visible rejection; both are whole-Run driver_failed faults with codes sdk_task_execution_route_authority_missing / catalog_execution_policy_unavailable (E1/E2), and the SDK unknown-tool WAITING path is unreachable. Foreground Runs always start ROUTED_TASK on the turn's scope with a projection frozen by that scope's root count, so 'create_new then write in the same Run' is impossible and, worse, a same-Run re-route makes the envelope attest a root the physical handler does not write into (E3, new P1). Auto mode already exempts every SDK tool authorization, not just folder append (new P1). Recommended design: keep AC-3 (1) PROJECT_EFFECT classification; implement the gate as ToolResult.rejected from ProductEffectExecutor with a frozen reason-code table and a frozen-authority consistency check; treat standalone/multi-root/hidden calls as documented fail-closed Run faults mapped by the Host to a durable FAILED with stable code (optionally reduce their probability with route-aware provider_specs hiding + tool_activate refusal, which keeps the catalog fingerprint stable); port confirm-only enforcement into decide() via explicit_only; and take D2 wording, TC-HM-09 step 6 multi-root canary, and post-append stale semantics to the user as a scope-change proposal.

The same per-turn-exposure limitation applies to task_scope_update: hiding it per turn cannot produce a model-visible rejection; calling it while hidden is a Run fault (catalog_execution_policy_unavailable), so the dirty/pending exposure design must also decide fault-vs-reject.

(2) Runs never start unbound: foreground_runtime.py:572-604 always injects a HOST_INITIAL RESUME_EXISTING receipt for the turn's task_scope_id (state starts ROUTED_TASK, react_loop.py:238-243), draft_lineage/prepare raise foreground_task_scope_authority_missing when task_scope_id is None (foreground_runtime_ports.py:91-92,114-115) and freeze raises foreground_tool_binding_authority_missing for binding_set_revision<1 (foreground_runtime_ports.py:306-311). (4) Hidden-tool calls are a pre-existing production hazard independent of S5b: every non-kernel tool is DEFERRED (tool_authority.py:75-95, foreground_runtime_ports.py:348-351) so a hallucinated un-activated tool name already fails the whole Run with catalog_execution_policy_unavailable; no Host/SDK test covers it (grep catalog_execution_policy_unavailable in backend/tests and simple-harness-sdk/tests: 0 hits).
findings.root_cause: The plan assigns the 'rejected' semantics of D2/AC-3 (1)(4) to an SDK preflight that only knows UNROUTED and same-batch barriers, and to a per-Run projection that is keyed by the frozen scope's root count rather than by route. Under the frozen SDK 0.7.1 the only Host-controllable model-visible rejection seam for a PROJECT_EFFECT call is AFTER issue_envelope succeeded (ProductEffectExecutor.execute returning EffectExecution(effect=None, ToolResult.rejected(...)) exactly like the SDK's own authorization-deny path at tools/executor.py:346-353); every case where issue_envelope or execution_policy must fail (standalone route, zero/multi root, hidden tool) is a whole-Run driver_failed. Required plan change: (a) drop plan.md:135 'SDK unknown-tool rejection' and plan.md:134 (5) as a rejection mechanism; state the partition explicitly: model-visible ToolResult.rejected = {UNROUTED, same-batch, forged authority field, EffectGate failures after envelope issue}; Run fault with stable code = {PROJECT_EFFECT under routed_standalone/memory_standalone -> sdk_task_execution_route_authority_missing, zero/multi root -> sdk_task_execution_root_authority_unavailable (or the new auditable reason), hidden/deferred tool -> catalog_execution_policy_unavailable}; (b) Host driver boundary maps those three codes to a durable FAILED observation with a user-facing message and the next turn (a new Run) is the recovery path — assert 'no execution_effects row, no host.file event, foreground FAILED with code' in the S5B-S4 lane; (c) optional probability reducer that keeps the catalog fingerprint stable: a Host RouteAwareExposure wrapper around CatalogRunToolExposure whose provider_specs(run_id) drops PROJECT_EFFECT specs while the ledger's current route for the Run is not ROUTED_TASK (route_state is already handed to prepare_snapshot via RunContextAuthorityRequest.route_state, context_authority.py:271-277; _tool_catalog_fingerprint reads checkpoint()['catalog_fingerprint'] so hiding does not touch the fingerprint) plus a refusal in the Host tool_activate handler for PROJECT_EFFECT capabilities outside ROUTED_TASK/project_bound with a model-visible stable code (activation results are ordinary tool results, runtime_catalog.py:1232-1244); (d) D2 wording must be amended to say that standalone-route project writes are hidden/non-activatable and, if still called, fail the turn closed with a stable reason instead of 'being rejected' and re-routed inside the same Run — this is acceptance text, so it needs user approval (see scope-change-proposal finding tc-hm-09-multi-root-canary-vs-oos-and-d2-wording).

conclusion.summary: Root causes of all three parents confirmed against the frozen SDK, the Memory wheel (0.6.0, two throwaway probes) and the v45 migration; two upgraded to P1 with definite fixes and one acceptance-wording scope-change-proposal added. Deterministic design: (1) ack INPUT = new Host tool `prospective_ack{occurrence_key}` (direct kernel, projectless-safe, default effect policy so it is exposed on all five routes), validated by exact membership of the 64-hex key the Host itself placed in the inbox message; terminal-based ack (option a) is rejected as input because it would mark refusals processed, but the acking run's terminal commit is the settled(acknowledged) driver. 'processed' must be redefined as 'durable prospective_ack receipt exists' (acceptance AC-4③/⑤ rewording needs user approval). (2) Canonical tables: Memory prospective_trigger_events/read_occurrence_inbox = occurrence identity; Host v46 prospective_occurrences = lifecycle claimed→presented→acknowledged→settled; v45 occurrence_presented = gate projection written ONLY when the occurrence leaves the mandatory inbox (ack or settled superseded/expired), in the same state.db transaction — never at snapshot injection, never for suppressed — which keeps the S5a read query and tests untouched and makes 'unacked → next turn still pending' and snapshot_hash_replay hold. (3) REGISTRATION_ACCEPTED (outbox-bound) is a hard prerequisite for any occurrence; Host must consume registration+invalidation outbox rows with a same-transaction cursor and deterministic signal identity so crash replays hit Memory's replay path instead of 'prospective_signal_replayed'/'stale'. (4) No Host signal can exit a triggered intent (EXPIRED is not_live after trigger); Memory-side completion is analysis-plan-only and Host settled(*) must be derived from inbox/outbox facts.

cross_cluster_refs.reason: task_scope_update / TaskScopeMutationPlan is NOT the ack carrier (frozen fields, absent on standalone routes); settled(acknowledged) should ride the same record_sdk_terminal terminal_commit_hooks seam that cluster owns, so the hook contract must accept a prospective settle writer alongside closure/outbox writers.

The prospective-occurrence fault lane runner (plan.md:46 does not exist yet) must inject at the two-database seams mapped here (Host tx1/tx2 around each Memory apply_prospective_signal, snapshot receipt, ack tool commit) and assert 'ignored' inbox rows are not claimed and 'prospective_signal_replayed' is handled.

The registration outbox only appears after the accepted plan is materialized (spike A2 step 4b) and read_outbox/read_occurrence_inbox reject the Host principal until the owner row is upgraded (spike A2 fact 10); the scheduler's outbox cursor loop is therefore blocked at cold start until Task 5's register_principal_owner lands — the scheduler must fail-closed (not fail-open) on short_horizon_principal_rejected.

findings.root_cause: presented→acknowledged has no deterministic input in the plan: acceptance defines ack by '终答提及' (NL judgement, forbidden), plan.md:169 points at a field that does not exist in the frozen TaskScopeMutationPlan and at a tool that is absent on memory_standalone/direct_standalone turns. Required fix (definite): add Host tool `prospective_ack` (strict schema {occurrence_key: 64-hex}; direct kernel; HOST_COMPOSED + PROJECTLESS_SAFE; default NON_PROJECT_EFFECT policy so it is exposed on every route) whose handler, in ONE state.db transaction, (i) verifies occurrence_key ∈ prospective_occurrences WHERE state='presented' for the local subject, (ii) CAS presented→acknowledged with run_id/provider_turn_ordinal/receipt, (iii) inserts the occurrence_presented projection row, (iv) writes an idempotent invocation row keyed (sdk_run_id, occurrence_key) so a lost-ACK replay returns the same receipt. 'processed' MUST mean 'a durable prospective_ack receipt exists for this occurrence_key' (or a Memory-side lifecycle exit/suppression/invalidation, see prospective-triggered-intent-has-no-host-exit); absence of the tool call — including refusal, silence, timeout, failed run — leaves the occurrence presented and re-presentable next turn. settled(acknowledged) is then driven deterministically by the acking run's terminal commit (terminal_commit_hooks) or, if that run never reaches terminal, by the next terminal that observes an acknowledged row.

findings.evidence: acceptance.md S5B-AC-4③ '模型终答未提及/拒绝 → 不标 processed' and ⑤ '模型终答提及 → ack' define the deterministic gate outcome by a natural-language property of the final answer. Program constraint (acceptance.md 矛盾分析 '不靠关键词' + primary finding) forbids keyword/regex/NL judgement, and no structured artefact of the frozen SDK carries the mention (see prospective-ack-channel-undefined). The sentence is therefore not verifiable as written by any deterministic oracle; only the manual_required real-provider lane S5B-S5 (quality_bar) can check the mention. Proposed replacement wording for user approval (D8): 'processed ⇔ durable `prospective_ack` receipt for the occurrence_key exists (Host tool, strict schema, exact membership check). No receipt — whether the model refused, ignored, timed out, or the Run failed — ⇒ occurrence stays presented and is re-presented next turn; no_recall stays blocked. findings.root_cause: The plan treats 'presented' as one fact stored twice; in reality the S5a gate consumes 'presented' as 'cleared from the mandatory inbox', which S5b's acceptance equates with 'processed'. Definite fix: (a) canonical Host lifecycle table = v46 `prospective_occurrences` (PK occurrence_key from Memory inbox; memory_id, prospective_revision, event_id, state ∈ claimed|presented|acknowledged|settled, settled_reason ∈ acknowledged|suppressed|superseded|expired, presented_run_id/snapshot_id, ack_run_id/ack_receipt, append-only event rows + monotonic head or event-sourced); (b) `occurrence_presented` (v45, schema untouched as plan.md:85 already says) becomes a pure GATE PROJECTION: its row is inserted only when the occurrence leaves the mandatory inbox — i.e. on acknowledged (prospective_ack commit) or on settled(superseded|expired) — in the SAME state.db transaction as the prospective_occurrences transition; it is never written at snapshot injection; suppressed occurrences never get a row (the reconcile predicate already drops suppressed entries, human_memory_v7.py:125-126, so no gate row is needed and the v45 CHECK is never hit). This keeps the S5a query and its receipted tests byte-identical and satisfies '未处理 → 下一轮继续 pending' and 'no_recall 只在 mandatory inbox 已清空后成立'. The column name presented_at then reads as 'cleared_at'; record that re-labelling in plan.md Task 6 and the v46 design freeze (Task 0) rather than adding columns to the v45 table. (c) claimed rows must be sourced from read_occurrence_inbox entries with outcome='matched' (never from the apply_prospective_signal result — see kill-point map), and the snapshot-injection step records presented_run_id/snapshot_id in prospective_occurrences in the same transaction as record_snapshot_receipt so replay stays hash-stable.

findings.evidence: UPGRADED P2→P1: the step is mandatory, not optional. sqlite_v5.py:5697-5705 calls _verify_live_prospective_registration_unlocked for every non-ack signal that is not stale/duplicate; :9628-9648 requires the newest prospective_scheduler_registrations row for (memory_id, target_revision, registration_revision, scheduler_registration_ref) to be state='accepted' with the same trigger_hash and no 'invalidated' row, else MemoryValidationError('prospective_scheduler_registration_not_live'). findings.root_cause: plan.md:169 ② goes straight from 'claim registration' to apply_prospective_signal(TIME_DUE/EVENT) and omits the REGISTRATION_ACCEPTED hand-shake and the identity discipline it implies. Definite fix for Task 6: (1) outbox consumption = one state.db transaction inserting prospective_scheduler_registrations(outbox_id PK, memory_id, prospective_revision, registration_revision, trigger_json, trigger_hash, payload_hash, state=received) AND advancing prospective_outbox_cursor (created_at, outbox_id) — '游标独立持久' in plan.md:169 must read 'own table, same transaction'; (2) then issue REGISTRATION_ACCEPTED with DETERMINISTIC identity derived from outbox_id (signal_id, signal_receipt_id/hash, scheduler_registration_ref, authority_id, nonce, operation_id all = stable hashes of outbox_id; observed_at = the durable received_at, not wall clock) or persisted in Host before the Memory call, so a crash-replay re-sends the same ref and hits Memory's replay path; treat 'prospective_signal_replayed' as terminal-already-accepted only after re-reading Memory's registration state; record state=accepted with the returned decision/result ids; (3) consume memory.prospective.invalidation.requested the same way with REGISTRATION_INVALIDATED (transition PENDING→PENDING on the OLD revision, outbox-bound) and mark the Host registration invalidated so tick never fires it again (AC-4② 'invalidation 后不再触发'); (4) tick issues TIME_DUE/EVENT_OCCURRED only for state=accepted registrations, with signal identity derived from (scheduler_registration_ref, event identity: clock bucket = trigger_at, or Host event id) so the Memory occurrence_key is reproducible across replays.

canonical_findings.root_cause: Refined root cause (parent confirmed). Memory 0.6.0 re-delivers the IDENTICAL MemoryAnalysisRequest only on lease reclaim / authority-transient retry of the same batch; every executor failure creates a new batch whose request_hash, attempt, job_id and idempotency_key all change while the evidence set stays the same (or grows). A Host ledger keyed only by (request_hash, attempt) therefore (a) correctly dedups reclaim/authority retries, but (b) cannot see a prior `sent_unknown` when Memory retries with attempt+1 -> blind resend of the same evidence set, violating ASSET-PROVIDER-IDEMPOTENCY. Second facet: with a non-streaming OpenAI-compatible chat/completions endpoint the provider response id is only known once the response arrived, the Host reconciliation adapter is a constant STILL_UNKNOWN and the SDK never replays, so `sent_unknown -> sent_confirmed` has NO executable production path; AC-2 (3)'s 'unknown then confirmed by provider response id' branch is exercisable only through an injected test reconciliation observer. Third facet: the plan's 30 s Memory lease is shorter than real analysis latency, so 0.6.0 will reclaim and re-deliver a request while the Host's provider call is still in flight; only a Host durable `handed_off` row (refuse/await, never re-dispatch) prevents a concurrent duplicate call. EXECUTABLE DESIGN the plan must state: (1) ledger table post_turn_invocation_attempts UNIQUE(request_hash, attempt) PLUS attempt-independent evidence_set_key = sha256(canonical(request.to_json() minus {job_id, attempt, idempotency_key})) PLUS a member index (subject, run_id, evidence_id, attempt_row_id) because membership grows between retries (probe P2); pre-dispatch rule: any member evidence with an open handed_off/sent_unknown row -> refuse without provider call. (2) Classification reuses Host dispatch handoff facts: transport not entered / ConnectTimeout -> not_sent (resend allowed as attempt+1); anything after handoff without a parsed response -> sent_unknown; parsed response persisted in the SAME transaction as state=succeeded together with provider_response_id/provider_response_hash (so there is no window in which a response exists but is not durable). (3) Terminal state of sent_unknown for this provider = Host executor raises a definite AnalysisAttemptBlocked(sent_unknown_unresolved) on every re-delivery (0 provider calls); Memory burns its retry schedule and dead-letters with last_error_code=analysis_executor_failed (probe P1b/P4); Host writes a durable event memory.analysis.blocked{reason, evidence_set_key} so the user-visible reason is not lost behind Memory's coarse code; raw evidence untouched (outbox row dead_letter, evidence_envelopes intact). Optional 0.6.1 addition (same wheel as Task 5): AnalysisExecutorPermanentError -> immediate dead_letter carrying the Host reason instead of N retries and N failed batch rows. (4) Confirm branch: keep `sent_confirmed` reachable only via an injected ProviderReconciliationObservation(COMPLETED) in the deterministic S5B-S3 lane; document that production has no confirm path. canonical_findings.root_cause: The plan treats 'presented' as one fact stored twice; in reality the S5a gate consumes 'presented' as 'cleared from the mandatory inbox', which S5b's acceptance equates with 'processed'. (c) claimed rows must be sourced from read_occurrence_inbox entries with outcome='matched' (never from the apply_prospective_signal result — see kill-point map), and the snapshot-injection step records presented_run_id/snapshot_id in prospective_occurrences in the same transaction as record_snapshot_receipt so replay stays hash-stable.

canonical_findings.evidence: V0 SPIKE-CROSS-DB-TRIGGER (spikes/run_protocol_spikes.py:292-388; manifests/spike-manifest.json fault_points registration_commit/occurrence_commit/snapshot_commit/ack_commit; required one_occurrence_per_revision_event, pending_not_lost, snapshot_hash_replay, suppression_fail_closed) modelled a single Host table `occurrences(state pending→presented→acknowledged, snapshot_hash)` + `event_cursor` with INSERT OR IGNORE. Mapping to the real two-database design (Memory human_memory_v7.db vs Host state.db, no cross-DB ACID — acceptance 同事务边界): registration_commit = {Memory: outbox row (already durable, never mutated)} → {Host tx1: prospective_scheduler_registrations(received)+cursor} → {Memory tx: REGISTRATION_ACCEPTED consumption+registration event} → {Host tx2: state=accepted}; kill between tx1 and Memory tx replays the same deterministic ref (probe A1 identical result); kill between Memory tx and tx2 with a non-deterministic ref yields 'prospective_signal_replayed' (probe A2) — Host must not treat that as failure. occurrence_commit = {Memory tx: TIME_DUE/EVENT → trigger_event(occurrence_key)+revision bump+invalidation outbox} → {Host tx: prospective_occurrences(claimed) sourced from read_occurrence_inbox outcome='matched'}; a Host crash after the Memory commit followed by a fresh-identity re-issue is NOT a duplicate occurrence (probe B2: outcome ignored/prospective_signal_stale, extra inbox row with outcome='ignored' that the predicate drops, exactly one 'matched' per revision) but a Host that wrote 'claimed' from the IGNORED result would create a phantom row — the claim MUST come from the inbox entry. snapshot_commit = {Host tx: run_context_snapshot_receipts + prospective_occurrences.presented(run_id, snapshot_id)}: because presented does not enter the reconcile predicate (gate projection is written only at ack/settle), replay of prepare_snapshot recomputes the same pending list (ordered by occurred_at,event_id, first 8) and record_snapshot_receipt is idempotent on (run, turn, payload_hash) → snapshot_hash_replay holds;
